title: FAD-KV: Adaptive Dictionary KV Caching for Efficient Reasoning Decoding
summary: Replaces dense per-token KV storage and prior dictionary-based sparse KV compression (OMP-style iterative coding, static or append-only dictionaries) with one-shot Top-n screening plus lightweight coefficient refinement and a fixed-size dictionary that recycles inactive atoms. Costs include maintaining and adapting the dictionary, per-step sparse coding and coefficient refinement, and integration complexity in the decode path; the abstract reports no memory-reduction factor or speedup. It can fail if screening misses the right atoms or stale atoms are reused under distribution shift, degrading long-reasoning quality, and reported quality-efficiency trade-offs may not transfer to a specific model or serving stack.
rationale: The mechanism targets exactly the reader's long-generation KV memory bottleneck on a single 24 GB GPU, but the abstract provides no quantified memory or latency claim and the method requires custom decode-path integration, so it should be tracked and benchmarked only if results mature rather than adopted now.
